verdict.rationale: Gram ships a first-party platform MCP server. Through it, an org admin in Claude Code, Cursor, Codex or another MCP client can add servers, build plugins, author skills, manage roles and risk policies, and read observability data in natural language without opening the dashboard. The language interpretation, however, comes from the user's external agent rather than a native command interface. The in-dashboard chat harness only tests MCP servers; it does not operate the platform. missing for 10: a native in-product natural-language command interface, documented coverage of the full management surface (e.g. deployments and billing via NL), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: An org admin working in Claude Code, Cursor, Codex, or another MCP client can find and add MCP servers, finish their setup, put them on a plugin, choose who receives a plugin, author skills, manage access roles, review shadow MCP servers, manage risk policies, configure telemetry delivery, and read observability data without opening the dashboard.
